prosody.lang: Legend says a man strapped on wings, jumped from this tower and flew across the Bosphorus. The Genoese built this tower. Back then Galata was a little walled town of Italian merchants, and the tower was the top of its walls. A cross stood on its peak, so it was called the Tower of the Holy Cross. In Ottoman times it became a fire watchtower. In a city of wooden houses, spotting a fire early could save a whole neighbourhood, so watchmen kept an eye on the city day and night. According to the traveller
, in the 17th century a scholar called
jumped from here with wings he had made himself, crossed the Bosphorus and landed in

" means "a thousand sciences". Legend says the sultan rewarded him, then grew afraid of such a man and sent him into exile. Nobody knows if he really flew. But when you reach the top, you'll see the view he saw. As you climb, think about it: for centuries Genoese merchants, Ottoman watchmen and Levantine families walked the streets below. The tower saw them all, and it is still standing guard over the city.
